question: The LCM of two numbers is 4158 and their HCF is 54. If one of the numbers is 378, what is the other number?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the property: Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

⇒ Other Number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ Given Number

⇒ Other Number = (4158 × 54) ÷ 378

⇒ Other Number = 4158 ÷ 7 (since 378 ÷ 54 = 7)

⇒ Other Number = 594

**∴ The correct answer is 594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 4158

HCF of the two numbers = 54

First number (N₁) = 378

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ 4158 × 54 = 378 × N₂

⇒ N₂ = (4158 × 54) ÷ 378

⇒ N₂ = (4158 × 54) ÷ (54 × 7)

⇒ N₂ = 4158 ÷ 7

⇒ N₂ = 594

**∴ The correct answer is 594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators. HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Product Rule Limitation

The standard formula (LCM × HCF = Product of numbers) is valid strictly for exactly two numbers. It does not hold true for three or more numbers.
